checked_sources: Frozen VERIFICATION.md and verification/verify_circular_sas.py, inspected without executing supplied code
Independent bounded replay: form the word for every admissible ordered gap tuple with 2≤k≤5 and directly test all binary targets through length k+1 at every indexed cut; 56 tuples and 612 cuts agreed
correctness.rationale: A cut just after a one partitions the word into k mixed blocks, so it is k-universal. Every length-(k+1) target with an adjacent 01 embeds by taking that pair in one block and one symbol in each remaining block. For a nonincreasing target 1^a0^(k+1−a), an embedding must double up on zeros in a long block after a blocks used for ones. Conversely, a long block of index at least a+1 makes this possible by using the first a blocks for the ones. Thus if h is the last long-block index, exactly the a from h to k+1 are absent. Reversal handles cuts immediately before ones. At a split long gap the alternating subsequence (01)^k0 has k mixed blocks and contains every length-(k+1) target except the all-ones word: greedy starts at index 1 or 2 and each change saves one position compared to a repeat. The terminal streak lengths contributed by each short-gap run of length r are 1 through r, once each on each side; zero streaks occur once per long gap on each side. This gives the claimed full histogram even for periodic words. For the Fibonacci images the cyclic source avoids 11 and 000, giving gaps 1 or 2 with no two short gaps adjacent. Letter counts determine both gap counts and are coprime, so indexed cuts there are distinct rotations.
residual_risks: The frozen output reports the larger k≤8 and Fibonacci m≤11 ranges; these were not independently replayed in full. Its 'necklaces' label counts ordered tuples, not 501 distinct cyclic equivalence classes. This does not affect the theorem or the number of checked indexed cuts across those tuples.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The missing implication is the symbolic evaluation across all cuts, including longer streaks. Neither a balance bound nor executing a general SAS algorithm establishes it. The specializations that coincide are not treated as distinct claims on the same formulas.

evidence: Resultary 0661c6ab7a7d and 29d94c67931e identify the same three-point histogram subject to isolated short gaps; 0661c6ab7a7d also has the exact same Fibonacci specialization.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: When r_i≤1, the arbitrary-run formula reduces to the corroborated three-point formula. At r_i≥2 it permits further multiplicities beginning at 4; replacing indexed cuts by distinct words for periodic inputs would also change the invariant.

originality.rationale: The distinct claim supported by the comparison is the complete indexed-cut law for arbitrary runs of short gaps, not an exclusive claim on the three-point law or the Fibonacci specialization. Two materially overlapping indexed records cover the no-adjacent-short-gap case; one gives the same Fibonacci histogram exactly. Neither supplies the arbitrary-run histogram. The inspected linear-word algorithms permit a per-cut calculation but do not state the cyclic aggregation.
residual_risks: Exact overlap in the restricted cases is material; dating alone neither establishes priority nor excludes a relationship. The comparisons do not exhaust alternate terminology or develop every possible corollary of general SAS theory.

checked_sources: Frozen Finding and proof, especially lines 8–24 and 36–52
value.rationale: For one necklace the least absent length does not distinguish any cuts; the number of witnesses at that length does. The complete invariant identifies why large multiplicities arise and shows that the order of the short-gap runs is immaterial, avoiding a per-rotation enumeration even for periodic words. The Fibonacci case is an illustrative specialization, not the main value beyond the exact subcase overlap.
residual_risks: Does not classify arbitrary gap lengths, and outside primitive words the histogram is for indexed cuts, not distinct rotations.
